plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: it maximizes expected profit regardless of what others bid, since you only pay the second-highest bid if you win. Bidding above value risks negative profit; bidding below value risks losing profitable auctions unnecessarily. With value $27, I will bid exactly $27 to ensure optimal outcomes in this single-round game.

In a second-price auction (winner pays second-highest bid), bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of opponents' strategies. This is because if I bid below my value, I risk losing auctions I could have profitably won; if I bid above my value, I risk winning at a price higher than my value, causing a loss. Since payment depends only on the second-highest bid (not my own bid, given I win), bidding exactly my value maximizes expected profit. With value $31, I will bid $31.

This is a second-price (Vickrey) auction where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of other bidders' strategies. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so bidding my true value of $20 maximizes my expected profit without risk of overpaying. Bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions; bidding higher risks winning at a loss. I will bid exactly my value.
